# Visualizing Amounts and Proportions

## Bar plots

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Appropriate for continuous-by-categorical data


:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-bar-bad", fig_bar_bad(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Bar plots

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Order matters (ascending or descending)
- Horizontal bars 
    - Often allow for longer labels
    - Fit better on standard pages
    - Worse on standard slides 


:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-bar-good", fig_bar_good(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Grouped bar plots

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Appropriate for continuous-by-categorical-by-categorical data
- Order matters (ascending or descending)
- Grouping matters - Bars you want to compare should be adjacent

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-bar-grouped", fig_bar_grouped(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Dot plots

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Appropriate for continuous-by-categorical data
- Use when you do not want an axis to start at zero
- Order still matters

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-dot", fig_dot(),
          w = 4.5, h = 7, x = 8, y = 1.5, width = 3.9)
place_fig("fig-bar-long", fig_bar_long(),
          w = 4.5, h = 7, x = 12, y = 1.5, width = 3.9)
```

## Heatmaps

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Appropriate for continuous-by-categorical-by-categorical data
- Map continuous values to color not position
- Best when there are many groups in each category and you are implying broad trends not precise values
- Order still matters
- Use sequential or diverging color scales that are colorblind safe

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-heatmap", fig_heatmap(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Pie charts

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Slice area = share of the whole
- Most useful with few categories and large percentages
- Works when the key message is a simple part-to-whole or majority comparison
- Example: SPD + FDP held a small majority over CDU/CSU

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-bundestag-pie", fig_bundestag_pie(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## When pie charts fail

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Five companies with similar shares (~20% each) over three years
- Pies: hard to compare shares within or across years
- Stacked bars: trends for A and E are visible, but middle bars shift across years
- Hard to compare anything but the bottom and top segments

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-marketshare-pies", fig_marketshare_pies(),
          w = 6.4, h = 2.3, x = 8.5, y = 1.2, width = 7.2)
place_fig("fig-marketshare-stacked", fig_marketshare_stacked(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 9.3, y = 4.3, width = 4.4)
```

## Side-by-side bars

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Best choice for comparing parts across groups
- Shared baseline makes values easy to compare within a year
- A and B grew; D and E shrank
- Facet by year to see change over time

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-marketshare-side-by-side", fig_marketshare_side_by_side(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Stacked bars with two categories

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Stacking works when there are only two parts per bar
- Women in the Rwandan parliament over time
- Dashed line at 50% shows when the majority flipped
- Side-by-side bars make the same data harder to read: the proportion is no longer visible as a whole

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-women-parliament", fig_women_parliament(),
          w = 5.5, h = 3.0, x = 9.2, y = 1.6, width = 5.6)
place_fig("fig-women-parliament-grouped", fig_women_parliament_grouped(),
          w = 5.5, h = 3.0, x = 9.2, y = 5.0, width = 5.6)
```
